newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco sold oil refineries stakes at $419 million.
newsitem.headline: Morocco sold oil refineries stakes at $419 million.

text.p: Morocco has sold majority stakes in oil refineries Samir and Societe Cherifienne des Petroles for a total of 3.9 billion dirhams ($419 million) to Saudi Corral Petroleum Holding AB, a minister said on Tuesday.
Privatisation Minister Abderrahman Saaidi told a news conference: "This was the greatest privatisation operation realised since 1993...It was a successful business."
Morocco has privatised 51 firms, including the two oil refineries, since the government launched its privatisation programme in 1993.
The Swedish-based Saudi Corrol Petroleum Holding AB bought 67.7 percent of Samir firm, Morocco's main oil refinery, at 3.5 billion dirhams, at the equivalent of 251 dirhams per share, Saaidi said.
It also bought 73.9 percent of SCP refinery at 473 million dirhams, or the equivalent of 365 dirhams per share, the minister told reporters.
The French oil company Elf holds 20 percent of SCP capital and Total holds three percent.

"Responding to the demand of Corral group, the Moroccan state will keep its holding at a level of 6.7 percent in Samir's capital and 7.39 percent in SCP for a period of 12 months to help the group adapt to the Moroccan oil market," Saaidi said.
Corral will purchase these stakes after the agreed 12 months, he added.
Workers also have a small stake in Samir.
"The Saudi group agreed to invest a total amount of (further) 3.8 billion dirhams in the oil sector and preserve domestic employment over a period of five years," the minister said.
The privatisation ministry floated 30 percent of Samir's capital on the Casablanca stock exchange at $310 million in March 1996.
Among the market's largest capitalisation firms, Samir has a capital of 1.032 billion dirhams, divided into 20.64 million shares of a 50 dirhams nominal value each.
The refinery made a net profit of 506 million dirhams in 1996, from 423 million dirhams in 1995.

Located in a 200 hectares (500 acre) site in Mohammedia on the Atlantic coast, near Morocco's financial centre of Casablanca, the Societe Maroccaine de l"Industrie de Raffinage has a capacity of 6.25 million tonnes per year or 80 percent of the country's needs of refined oil products.
The company, founded in 1959, has also a storage capacity of nearly 900,000 cu metres for crude oil and 870,000 cu metres for refined oil.

SCP refinery, located in the central town of Sidi Kacem, has a capital of 245 million dirhams, and refines an estimated 20 percent of Morocco's oil products. It made a net profit of 180 million dirhams in 1996, from 80 million dirhams the previous year.

The ministry said Corral group holds 100 percent in Swedish Preem Petroleum firm which has 550 distribution stations throughout Sweden. It has also two oil refineries in the country with a total capacity of 300,000 barrels per day.
